messages:
alice_support: Opening an escalation for ACME corp — customer noticed ~2x charge on invoice vs live dashboard. They say requests retried after an auth timeout and they see duplicate completions. Attaching short excerpt from their client log.

raul_account: Oof. Do we have invoice IDs / customer_id? we should pause any further billing analytics for them while we investigate.

alice_support: customer_id: acct_0ACME, invoice: inv_2026_03_10_042, they included this client log: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:07Z] send req id=abc123 idempotency_key=eyJ.. ttl=30s token=expiring
[2026-03-10T14:12:37Z] auth refresh started for token expiring
[2026-03-10T14:12:38Z] client saw timeout, retried req id=abc123 idempotency_key=eyJ..
[2026-03-10T14:12:38Z] server accepted new connection; inbound headers missing Idempotency-Key
[2026-03-10T14:12:38Z] gateway forwarded request -> served completion (cost ~1150 tokens)
[2026-03-10T14:12:38Z] client received success for original request later
```
They say the dashboard shows 1.15M tokens but invoice is ~2.3M.

brian_infra: Gateway logs for that window? I can grep the ingress cluster for id=abc123.

gateway-bot: deploy/ingress-gw-4 reported connection reset for 10.10.22.45 -> initiating retry policy (policy: client_timeout_replay). Request meta: src=10.10.32.100 dst=model-cluster-2

brian_infra: ✅ grep results: I see two distinct ledger writes for trace `abc123` with different request_ids: rq-A and rq-B. First write shows idempotency_key=null. Second write has idempotency_key=eyJ..

claire_billing: If there are two ledger writes both charged that could explain ~2x. Can you paste the ledger rows? We should confirm whether both reached billing pipeline.

brian_infra: ledger rows (redacted): 
```
write ts=2026-03-10T14:12:38Z req_id=rq-A account=acct_0ACME model=gpt-rare tokens=1150 idempotency_key=null
write ts=2026-03-10T14:12:39Z req_id=rq-B account=acct_0ACME model=gpt-rare tokens=1150 idempotency_key=eyJ..
```
Both ended up in the ingestion topic.

dmitry_sre: This smells like header strip during auth refresh path. If the proxy re-auths the connection it might reconstruct headers and drop the idempotency header in one branch. Also client TTL for idempotency might be too short relative to refresh delay.

jen_mobile_sdk: Our mobile SDK sets idempotency TTL=30s by default and reuses idempotency_key across retries. However we have a codepath where during token refresh we reinitialize the request object which can drop headers if the SDK sees an auth error and does a fresh send. I will check the exact client stack trace they provided.

alice_support: Customer is asking for immediate refund if double-charged. We should also provide mitigation steps they can do client-side.

claire_billing: Can we determine whether both writes were billed? I can run a quick query against billing ingestion to see if rq-A and rq-B were both consumed. If yes, we should prepare a credit.

brian_infra: Query result: both records consumed by the metering consumer and both produced invoice line items. Consumer offset shows both accepted.

dmitry_sre: Root cause hypothesis: gateway retry triggered during auth refresh -> one path dropped Idempotency-Key header -> backend treated it as a new request -> both entries were produced -> billing double-charge.

brian_infra: Repro steps I used locally: 
1) Start client request with short-lived token (TTL 15s) and idempotency header.
2) Force token refresh by rejecting auth on subsequent keepalive.
3) Gateway applies retry policy and replays request but due to reauth path the header is omitted.
4) Two ledger events observed.

jen_mobile_sdk: On our end: we can increase idempotency TTL to 2m and add retry jitter/backoff. Also will patch SDK to avoid reinitializing request object on refresh so header persists. I can cut a patch today.

brian_infra: On infra: will patch gateway to preserve Idempotency-Key through the auth refresh path and add a test. Also adding a short-lived check: if ledger sees two writes with same account+model+tokens within 1s and one has idempotency_key null and another non-null, mark for manual billing review rather than auto-accept.

claire_billing: I'll open a billing-credit PR for acct_0ACME for the duplicate 1150-token line items once SRE confirms scope. For now I'll flag invoice inv_2026_03_10_042 for review.

alice_support: Customer updated: they can provide more trace IDs if needed. They asked: is there any mitigation they can do immediately?

dmitry_sre: Immediate mitigations for customers: 
- Increase idempotency key TTL in SDK/config to 2m
- Set client-side retry only after explicit non-2xx errors and with exponential backoff
- Avoid client-side hard timeouts less than token refresh window

brian_infra: Action items: 
- jen_mobile_sdk: patch and release v1.4.2 with header persistence (ETA: 6h)
- infra: patch gateway auth-refresh header preservation + unit test (ETA: 24h)
- billing: prepare credit and hold invoice (claire)
- support: keep customer in loop and collect other trace IDs (alice)

claire_billing: Starting credit workflow now — setting tentative credit and awaiting SRE confirmation.

alice_support: Thanks all. I'll update the customer with the mitigation steps and expected timeline. :thumbsup:

gateway-bot: incident-tracker logged issue INF-7620 (label: billing-dup-after-retry). Assigned -> brian_infra, jen_mobile_sdk, dmitry_sre.

brian_infra: I'll follow up with a postmortem after we close the loop.

alice_support: Last note from customer: they saw this pattern ~3x in the last month but only this invoice doubled. I'll collect more traces and add to the thread.
